# The Problem

Tertiary analysis is the step after variant calling and filtering. A researcher has a few hundred germline variants from a rare disease family, a hereditary cancer panel or a population study, and needs to know for each one: how common is it in gnomAD, what does ClinVar say, what does it do to the transcript and the protein. The people who do this in R are geneticists, clinical research bioinformaticians and computational biologists in small groups, often one person per lab. The lead applicant's lab does this for rare and undiagnosed disease cases, and every case repeats the same joins by hand.

The R side is mature at the bottom and missing in the middle. VariantAnnotation reads VCF files into VRanges and GRanges objects and predicts coding consequences [@obenchain2014]. VariantFiltering and TVTB filter and summarise. ensemblVEP wraps the Ensembl VEP tool, which must be installed locally with Perl. myvariant queries MyVariant.info. The MafDb packages carry gnomAD allele frequencies for one release each. vaRHC and AutoGVP classify variants under ACMG rules and need annotated input. plyranges gives ranges a dplyr grammar, and the tidyomics ecosystem extends it to bulk, single cell and spatial data [@hutchison2024]. The web resources have moved to APIs: gnomAD has a GraphQL API, Ensembl VEP has a REST endpoint, and ClinVar is reachable through E-utilities and MyVariant.info.

Three things do not exist, checked on 2026-10-01.

1. There is no variant package in the tidyomics ecosystem. The organisation holds plyranges, plyinteractions, tidybulk, tidySummarizedExperiment, tidySingleCellExperiment, tidySpatialExperiment, tidydeseq2 and tidyprint. A variant table that behaves like a tibble and still converts to VRanges is missing.
2. There is no R implementation of the GA4GH Variation Representation Specification (VRS) [@wagner2021]. VRS 2.0 defines how to normalize an allele and compute a stable identifier for it, so that ClinVar, gnomAD, ClinGen and a local VCF join on one key with no HGVS parsing and no build-specific string matching. The reference implementation is vrs-python. A GitHub search for VRS code in R returns nothing.
3. No R package records where an annotation came from. When a table says a variant is pathogenic, nothing in it says ClinVar release 2026-08, retrieved 2026-09-14, queried by rsID. The analysis cannot be rerun against the same release, and a reviewer cannot audit the call.

The cost is repeated glue code in every group: key normalization, joins with different column names per source, and some way of remembering the release. Solving this gives R users an exact join key across resources, a table that works with dplyr and Bioconductor at the same time, and a provenance record that makes a variant table reproducible. It also gives tidyomics its missing data type and a GA4GH standard its first R implementation.
